speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with fever and altered mentation for two days; to guide my assessment, are you currently experiencing severe headache, neck stiffness, or a rash?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS)

Based on your history of taking haloperidol, your altered mental status, and fever, this clinical picture strongly suggests Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, a life-threatening reaction to antipsychotic drugs. I need to see your vital signs and request a Complete Blood Count and Creatine Kinase (CK) levels immediately to confirm this diagnosis.
